rubric.why: Newlands arranged elements by increasing atomic mass.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the elements were arranged in order of increasing atomic mass or atomic weight.

rubric.why: This arrangement placed elements with similar properties at every eighth position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that every eighth element had properties similar to the first, or naming the law of octaves.

modelAnswer: Newlands arranged the elements in order of increasing atomic masses.
He observed that every eighth element had properties similar to the first, like notes in an octave.

items.followUp: Define atomic radius and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: The definition identifies the distance from the nucleus to the atom’s outermost shell (or the equivalent half-distance between adjacent nuclei).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition of atomic radius.

rubric.why: The SI unit of length, and therefore of atomic radius, is the metre.

modelAnswer: Atomic radius is the distance from the centre of an atom’s nucleus to its outermost electron shell.
Its SI unit is the metre (m).

items.followUp: Explain how a coordinate covalent bond forms in the hydronium ion, H₃O⁺.

rubric.why: Nitrogen in ammonia has a lone pair of electrons available for donation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the lone pair on nitrogen in NH₃.

rubric.why: Nitrogen donates its lone pair to H⁺, forming the coordinate bond in NH₄⁺.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the lone pair is donated to H⁺ to form a coordinate covalent bond.

modelAnswer: The nitrogen atom in NH₃ has a lone pair of electrons.
It donates this pair to H⁺, forming a coordinate covalent bond and producing NH₄⁺.

items.followUp: What are intramolecular forces? Give one example.

rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining intermolecular forces as forces between molecules.

rubric.why: A valid example illustrates a force acting between molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example, such as hydrogen bonding between water molecules.

modelAnswer: Intermolecular forces are forces of attraction between molecules.
For example, hydrogen bonds attract neighbouring water molecules.

items.followUp: Give two differences between ionic and covalent compounds.

rubric.why: Polar compounds have unequal charge distribution and a dipole; non-polar compounds do not have a permanent dipole.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly contrasting the charge distribution or dipole moment of polar and non-polar compounds.

rubric.why: The solubility of each type generally follows the polarity of the solvent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that polar compounds dissolve in polar solvents and non-polar compounds in non-polar solvents.

modelAnswer: Polar compounds have partial positive and negative ends (a dipole); non-polar compounds do not have a permanent dipole.
Polar compounds generally dissolve in polar solvents, whereas non-polar compounds generally dissolve in non-polar solvents.

rubric.why: Platinum is used to make jewellery and ornaments.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming jewellery or ornaments as a use of platinum.

rubric.why: Platinum is used as a catalyst and also in certain electrical or laboratory applications.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming a valid second use, such as a catalyst, electrical contacts, or laboratory apparatus.

modelAnswer: Platinum is used for making jewellery.
It is used as a catalyst in chemical reactions.

items.followUp: Calculate the mass-by-mass percentage of a solution containing 5 g of solute in 100 g of solution.

rubric.why: The definition compares the mass of solute with the total mass of solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying mass of solute and mass of solution in the ratio.

rubric.why: Mass/mass percentage is the mass of solute divided by mass of solution, multiplied by 100.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula or equivalent definition.

modelAnswer: Mass-by-mass percentage is the mass of solute present in 100 parts by mass of solution.

items.followUp: Define a suspension and state one property that distinguishes it from a colloid.

rubric.why: A colloid is a heterogeneous mixture with one substance dispersed through another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining a colloid as a heterogeneous mixture of dispersed particles and a dispersion medium.

rubric.why: Colloidal particles are typically between 1 nm and 1000 nm in size.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the colloidal particle-size range of approximately 1–1000 nm.

modelAnswer: A colloidal solution is a heterogeneous mixture in which particles of one substance are dispersed throughout another substance.
The size of colloidal particles is approximately 1 nm to 1000 nm.
